keyVerseText: Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun בֹּהֶן (bôhen) originates from an unused root likely meaning 'to be thick,' which aligns with the physical characteristic of a thumb or great toe as being thicker or more substantial parts of the hand and foot. This etymological insight deepens our understanding beyond the simple English gloss of 'thumb' or 'great toe,' highlighting these digits as prominent, strong, and essential extremities. The term consistently refers to these two digits together, emphasizing their paired symbolic and functional significance in the body.
usageInScripture: The word בֹּהֶן appears sixteen times in the Hebrew Bible, always referring collectively to the thumb and great toe. The dominant translation is 'and upon the great toe,' occurring twelve times, with two instances in the plural form 'great toes,' and two instances referring to 'his thumbs' or 'having their thumbs.' This consistency in usage, especially in ritual contexts as seen in Exodus and Leviticus, underscores the importance of these specific extremities in ceremonial acts, often paired together to symbolize completeness or wholeness in the human body.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the use of בֹּהֶן to denote the thumb and great toe in sacred rituals points to the comprehensive nature of consecration and dedication to God. These digits represent the extremities of the body—both hand and foot—symbolizing the entirety of a person's actions and walk in life being set apart for the Lord. In the Christian faith, this holistic consecration prefigures the believer’s total surrender to Christ, where every part of life, from deeds (hand) to journey (foot), is sanctified. Recognizing the original Hebrew term enriches our appreciation for the detailed care God commands in worship and the profound symbolism embedded in His instructions.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 29:20 commands the priestly consecration ritual where blood is applied to the tip of the right ear, thumb, and great toe, including the בֹּהֶן. The inclusion of the thumb and great toe in this rite signifies the setting apart of both the priest’s ability to act (hand) and to walk (foot) in service to God. This word, bôhen, thus anchors the verse’s meaning in the physical and spiritual dedication of the priest’s whole person, underscoring the comprehensive nature of God’s call to holiness.
